data.body:
Landed as Gerrit change 1741 (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1), merged to main as afe33d3e70.

CONTRIBUTING.md section 2d is the authoritative wording, placed in the iterate-on-findings step because that is where an author is by definition holding a change with known findings. Both spellings are given (%wip at push time, POST /a/changes/<n>/wip on an existing change), both release paths, and the rationale: both votes green is a statement about the gates, never about whether the author thinks it is done. The packaged code-review guide mirrors it so rebar explain review carries it, and AGENTS.md has a one-line pointer.

The test asserts the guide through the packaged registry mapping (registry.explain_guide) rather than the file path — a path assertion would still pass if the guide stopped being packaged, and the packaged surface is the one that has to carry the rule. Deletion check verified: removing the %wip sentence from CONTRIBUTING.md reds the suite.

This batch exercised the rule on itself twice. Change 1731 was stacked on a change whose Verified was still pending, and I declined to submit the stack top because that would have landed an ungated ancestor — the same failure shape as 1727. And when 1731 kept drawing a macOS flake, the stack was re-parented so the healthy changes could land independently rather than being held hostage.
